findings.title: Nil http.Client causes a panic on every call
findings.evidence: The function accepts a client pointer and immediately dereferences it via client.Do(req) without any nil guard, so a caller passing nil reaches a runtime panic instead of a returned error.
findings.recommendation: Either reject nil explicitly with a returned error before use, or default to http.DefaultClient when client is nil.

findings.title: Responses larger than 1 MiB are silently truncated and reported as success
findings.evidence: The body is read through io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxBody) and then returned directly, so any 200 OK response exceeding maxBody is cut off at 1 MiB with no error to the caller.
findings.recommendation: Use http.MaxBytesReader-style enforcement or read maxBody+1 bytes and return an explicit error when the response exceeds the limit, so callers never treat truncated content as complete.
